# TraderSwift

TraderSwift is the infrastructure layer for agentic trading. Guides and build notes.

Site: https://blog.traderswift.io

Static HTML and Markdown.

## Guides

- [What is Signer, and who is it for?](signer-guides/01-what-is-signer.html) | Markdown: signer-guides/01-what-is-signer.md | Signer lets an agent trade from a key that no one holds whole, under a policy the owner writes on a chain.
- [How does an order get signed?](signer-guides/02-how-does-an-order-get-signed.html) | Markdown: signer-guides/02-how-does-an-order-get-signed.md | The path of one order from an agent's request to the venue, and the decision record it leaves on the chain.
- [How do I try Signer on my own computer?](signer-guides/03-how-do-i-try-signer-on-my-own-computer.html) | Markdown: signer-guides/03-how-do-i-try-signer-on-my-own-computer.md | Build the chain and the signer node on your own machine and start a throwaway local network, with no venue and no real key.
- [How do I write a trading policy?](signer-guides/04-how-do-i-write-a-trading-policy.html) | Markdown: signer-guides/04-how-do-i-write-a-trading-policy.md | The fields a Signer policy has today, what Policy v2 plans to add, what stays with you, and a prompt to draft one from your own history.
- [How do I stop an agent fast?](signer-guides/05-how-do-i-stop-an-agent-fast.html) | Markdown: signer-guides/05-how-do-i-stop-an-agent-fast.md | Revoke the policy on the Signer chain and every later order from that delegate is refused.
- [How do I read Signer's record?](signer-guides/06-how-do-i-read-signers-record.html) | Markdown: signer-guides/06-how-do-i-read-signers-record.md | Run a read-only node from the public genesis file and look at policies and decision records, signed and refused.
- [How do I run a Signer validator?](signer-guides/07-how-do-i-run-a-signer-validator.html) | Markdown: signer-guides/07-how-do-i-run-a-signer-validator.md | Build the chain binary, sync a node and join the validator set by rule, yourself or with your own agent following SKILL.md.
- [How do I launch a node with one link?](signer-guides/08-how-do-i-launch-a-node-with-one-link.html) | Markdown: signer-guides/08-how-do-i-launch-a-node-with-one-link.md | Give your own agent one link, say "Go" once, and it launches, seals and leaves. Planned.
- [How do I run my own Signer chain?](signer-guides/09-how-do-i-run-my-own-signer-chain.html) | Markdown: signer-guides/09-how-do-i-run-my-own-signer-chain.md | Build the Signer chain from the public code and run your own network, with your own admin. Anchoring to the hub is planned.
- [How do I get a Signer key for my own account?](signer-guides/10-how-do-i-get-a-signer-key-for-my-own-account.html) | Markdown: signer-guides/10-how-do-i-get-a-signer-key-for-my-own-account.md | Outsiders can't get a key yet. What it will take, and the milestones to get there. Planned.
- [How do I hold my own key shares?](signer-guides/11-how-do-i-hold-my-own-key-shares.html) | Markdown: signer-guides/11-how-do-i-hold-my-own-key-shares.md | Two shares on your machines, one on the network, so the network alone can never sign. Planned.
- [How do I run a private Signer network on ESP32s?](signer-guides/12-how-do-i-run-a-private-signer-network-on-esp32s.html) | Markdown: signer-guides/12-how-do-i-run-a-private-signer-network-on-esp32s.md | A household quorum: ESP32s approve each order, two Raspberry Pis hold the shares. Planned.
- [Signer – How to Run, Test and Trade with It](signer-guides/index.html) | Markdown: signer-guides/index.md | Twelve how-tos for people interested in Signer, each with steps and prompts for your own agent. Some are planned, and say so.
